title: City Ember-Resistant Zone (Zone Zero/0) Policy / Compliance, Implementatoin, and Current City Code Analysis / Cost of Compliance for Owners and City Outreach and Enforcement / Exemptions / AB 3074 / SB 504 / AB 1455 / Executive Order N-18-25
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Chief Legislative Analyst (CLA) and the City Administrative Officer (CAO), with assistance from the Office of the City Attorney, the Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD), and the Department of Building and Safety (LADBS), to report back in 60 days on the variables regarding the City’s own version of the Zone 0 policy the City Council must decide prior to the drafting of an implementation ordinance including the deadline by which the City must adopt its own regulations. This report will also include an analysis of CF 25-1428’s compliance with the alternative practices language in the final Zone 0 rule package submitted to the Office of Administrative Law and whether the integration of additional home hardening requirements into the City’s Zone 0 policy could allow the City to take a different approach to well-maintained vegetation remaining in the mandated “ember resistant zone” while achieving the required “substantially similar practical effects”. SEP 1 6 2026 I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct the CLA and CAO, with assistance from the Office of the City Attorney, LAFD, and LADBS, to report back in 60 days with an analysis of current City code and regulations applicable to landscaping and structures in the VHFHSZ including but not limited to current City brush clearance requirements, existing landscaping requirements for new construction, adopted and proposed California Wildland Urban Interface Code, adopted and proposed International Wildland Urban Interface Code, and current building code. This analysis will address how these regulations layer with one another and how they would integrate with proposed Zone 0 requirements. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct the CLA and CAO, with the assistance of the Community Forest Advisory Committee (CFAC), to report back in 60 days on the estimated cost of compliance for property owners across the City Los Angeles, including a distinction between estimated costs for single family homes, multifamily homes, and commercial properties, and resources available to property owners to fund the work necessary to comply with the new Zone 0 regulations including resources for home hardening not required by current Zone 0 regulations. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct the CAO and CLA, with the assistance of the General Services Department (GSD), the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP), the Los Angeles Zoo, and the Department of Recreation and Parks (RAP), to report back in 60 days on the estimated cost of Zone 0 compliance for properties owned by the City of Los Angeles. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct the CLA and CAO, with assistance from the Department of City Planning’s Office of Historic Resources, LADBS, and LAFD, to report back in 60 days on recommendations for a policy providing exemptions from Zone 0 requirements for historically and culturally significant structures or gardens with adequate fire suppression systems. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct the CAO and CLA, with the assistance of CFAC, LAFD, and LADBS, to report back in 60 days on the anticipated cost of outreach and enforcement necessary for successful implementation of the Zone 0 requirements. PRESENTED BY: Ma _ • SECONDED BY: TRACI PARK Councilwoman, 11th District
